title: Cutting a gene and a vector with the same enzyme
caption: EcoRI recognises GAATTC, which reads the same on both strands, and cuts each strand between the G and the A, leaving single-stranded AATT overhangs. Cut with the same enzyme, the gene's ends and the vector's ends all fit each other, and DNA ligase seals them, restoring the site at both joins.
alt: A gene with two EcoRI sites cut into three fragments and a vector with one site cut open, each with sticky overhangs, then the middle gene fragment ligated into the vector, with the GAATTC site restored at both joins.
description: EcoRI recognises GAATTC and cuts between G and A on each strand.
The staggered cut leaves 5′ overhangs of AATT, called sticky ends.
The gene has two sites, so it gives three fragments; the middle one is the gene to be cloned.
The vector has one site and is cut open.
AATT pairs with AATT on another EcoRI-cut molecule, so the gene fits into the vector and ligase seals the backbones; GAATTC is restored at both joins.
